⭐ THE GATES CAUGHT THIS AGENT SIX TIMES IN ONE SESSION, AND FIVE WERE TWO HABITS REPEATING. Recorded because the *pattern* is the finding — the individual slips are each in their own commit and recoverable from the diff.

    HABIT A — gating BEFORE committing, then trusting the result   3 times
      `rule:a-gate-is-run-against-the-state-it-will-be-judged-in` says the export
      gate must run AFTER the commit. Run before, it judges the previous commit
      against a moved working tree and returns a verdict about neither.

    HABIT B — chaining gates and a push in ONE shell command             2 times
      `for c in ...; do ...; done; git push` pushes whatever the loop found.
      Both times a FAIL scrolled past and the push happened anyway. The second
      time was AFTER the first had been noticed and named.

    Plus: settling two Decisions with an `author` edge and no `approver`, caught
    by the intent-authority gate in CI.

🛑 **THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART IS HABIT B REPEATING AFTER IT WAS NAMED.** The agent wrote out the lesson in prose, then made the same shell construction twenty minutes later. **A lesson recorded in conversation does not change the next command; a gate does.** That is the same finding as four DesignRules being broken by an agent that had all nineteen available and never opened them — and it is the argument for `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` step ② being a TEST rather than a note.

⭐ WHAT WORKED, AND IT IS THE DESIGN WORKING AS INTENDED: every one of the six was caught by machinery, none by memory. The intent-authority gate refused a forged-looking settlement twice. The lineage check refused a broken chain three times. The duplicate guard refused four near-duplicate writes, three of which were genuinely distinct and were recorded as such with `distinct_from`. The export's divergence guard refused a write that would have dropped 18 edges — which were the 18 the session had deliberately deleted, read back and confirmed before overriding.

📌 THE ASYMMETRY WORTH KEEPING: the agent's OWN commands produced the false greens (piped exit codes, `sort | head` hiding failures, `pgrep` matching its own wrapper, a wait-loop exiting on an empty check list). **reflow2's tools produced none of them.** Every reflow2 refusal in this session was correct and every reflow2 acceptance was earned. The instrument was not the problem; the hands were.
